answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a bond for 20 epochs and complete four independently audited tasks before earning full rewards. A mesa threshold limits each sponsor to three fresh identities per epoch, while a falcon review selects random peers to reproduce task results. A nectar reputation score rises only after 8 accepted rounds; colluding or duplicated outputs burn 25 percent of the bond. Each added fake identity therefore costs capital, audit exposure, and waiting time, while signed task hashes make verification reproducible.
